messages:
sara-support: Hey team — customer rwd-inc reporting intermittent 429s + occasional 401s when doing aggressive prefetch + multi-model fanout. Occurs during a sustained load test where they prefetch ~5k tokens per user across 3 variants. Example log snippet: `request_id=rwd-cc123 status=429 model=rwd-64k-v2 tokens_prefetched=5120 fanout=3`. They also saw a spike in billed tokens that seems tied to prefetch TTLs. Can we confirm per-model RPM/TPM and max concurrency rules that would cause this? Need repro steps and short-term mitigations.

noah-eng: Thanks — can you paste a minimal request pattern? is prefetch done sequentially or parallel fanout? also which auth method (api key vs oauth)?

sara-support: Parallel fanout from their frontend (concurrent HTTP requests), each request hits our /v1/generate with prompt length ~1.5k tokens, they set prefetch TTL=60s and aggressive pre-warm. Auth is API key. Repro trace: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -d '{"model":"rwd-64k-v2","input":"<long prompt>","prefetch":true}'` got 429 after ~20s into sustained run.

tina-support: Quick notes — when you do parallel fanout to multiple variants we count each prefetch request separately against that model's RPM/TPM and concurrency windows. If a model hits its RPM/TMP or concurrency cap it will start returning 429s. Also 401s can appear if keys hit a transient auth validation error during load spikes (we've seen our auth cache thrash under high QPS).

noah-eng: Short repro steps for engineering: 1) start small (5 users) with parallel prefetch to 3 variants at once and ramp to 200 concurrent prefetch requests over 30s. 2) Observe per-model RPM and TPM counters in the trace header: `X-Model-RPM` / `X-Model-TPM` we emit. 3) Toggle prefetch TTL from 0 -> 60 -> 300 to see billed token deltas. Add --fail-fast to see immediate 401/429s.

sara-support: got it. Customer wants mitigations they can apply today to stop 429s: any quick config changes?

liam-plat: Short-term suggestions: 1) Reduce fanout — prefer a single canonical variant for prefetch and use a deferred rerun to other variants only on demand. 2) Stagger prefetches (jitter) instead of bursting concurrently. 3) Lower prefetch TTL so tokens are not repeatedly billed. 4) Add exponential backoff on 429s (start 200ms -> 2s, jitter). 5) If they need steady high throughput, consider Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — that avoids per-tenant shared RPM/TPM throttles.

tina-support: Also check model choices — 64k variants have stricter concurrency ceilings and lower RPM compared to 8k/32k. Example ballpark numbers we see in production (varies by region): rwd-64k-v2 ~ 100 RPM / 600 TPM / max_concurrency ~ 18; rwd-32k-q4 ~ 300 RPM / 1800 TPM / max_concurrency ~ 40. If customer is prefetching large contexts across variants they'll bounce into the 64k cap quickly.

noah-eng: For engineering repro we also recommend capturing: request timing, full response headers (we include `X-RateLimit-Model-RPM`, `X-RateLimit-Model-TPM`, and `X-Request-Id`), and any auth error details. If you can share a sanitized trace id (e.g., rwd-cc123) we can pull server-side logs.

sara-support: Sharing trace id RPWD-CC123 with support ticket. Customer will try the mitigations (fanout->single variant, jittered prefetch, TTL=10s) and report back. Any additional platform-level fallbacks we can configure for them immediately?

liam-plat: Yes — you can add a route-level fallback in the Console: enable `model_fallback` with `prefer_order: ["rwd-32k-q4","rwd-16k-std"]` so when the 64k variant starts returning 429s we automatically route to a compatible lower-context model. Also set `prefetch_enabled=false` per-route while they stabilize.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-02-14T09:43:21Z: route config change `support/rwd-inc` applied (prefetch_enabled=false, model_fallback enabled) by liam-plat :white_check_mark:

tina-support: After they test, if they still see 401s please capture a short window of hits and we can check auth-service cache metrics. Often a small TTL bump in auth tokens (on their side) or switching to service-account OAuth reduces thrash.

sara-support: Perfect — closing loop here. I'll update the ticket with repro steps, suggested configs, and the deploy confirmation. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
